_readme: Application (app-only) permissions considered highly privileged for this audit, grouped by resource appId. Critical is reserved for a direct or 1-2 hop path to tenant takeover; service-specific or data-plane permissions that need additional prerequisites are High. 'severity' is either 'Critical' or 'High'. Edit freely: add/remove roles or whole resources. Matching is done by permission value against each resource's appRoles, so entries here are tenant-agnostic and safe to reuse across environments.

checks._readme: Check-run configuration for the attack-surface audit. 'enabled' toggles individual checks (empty = all on), 'min_severity' drops findings below a level (Critical/High/Medium/Low/Info), 'suppress' silences findings by 'check_id:primary_object_id' (or just 'check_id' to drop a whole check).

directory_roles._readme: Directory role displayName -> severity (Critical/High/Medium/Low/Info) for the privileged-users check. Critical is reserved for a direct or 1-2 hop path to tenant takeover; broader administrative roles are High. Roles not listed here (or custom roles) render as Info until you rate them. Add/modify freely per tenant.

role_labels._readme: Short human labels (permission value -> label) shown as the role description in the drawer's role tables, e.g. 'Application.ReadWrite.All': 'Read and write all applications'. The tool ships sensible defaults for well-known catalog permissions; add or override entries here per tenant.

roles.reason: Assign any Entra directory role to any principal. Direct path to Global Administrator.
Grant any Graph app role to any service principal without an admin-approval workflow. Chain: grant self RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory, then assign Global Administrator.
Add credentials to any app or SP and modify app properties — hijack high-privilege apps. A standard tenant-takeover primitive.
Create and configure federated domains. Combined with Hybrid Identity Administrator this enables Golden SAML without on-prem ADFS.
Assign the Global Administrator role to a controlled user account by creating an active PIM role assignment.
Add authentication methods, such as a Temporary Access Pass, to any non-privileged user - direct account takeover when granted as an app role.
Read and write directory data, including setting group memberships. Cannot directly manage role assignments or add users to role-assignable groups.
Modify user properties, managers, and profile data. Does not include password reset.
Add/remove members from any security group; add self to groups with ARM RBAC assignments. Cannot modify role-assignable groups — those require RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory.
Create or modify Conditional Access policies: disable MFA for specific users or apps and create exclusions for the attacker identity.
Push Intune device configuration/compliance policies fleet-wide. Combined with DeviceManagementScripts.ReadWrite.All: code execution on managed workstations and PAWs.
Deploy scripts to Intune-managed devices. Combined with DeviceManagementConfiguration.ReadWrite.All: fleet-wide code execution on managed workstations and PAWs.
Can add members to any group except for role-assignable groups.
Can manage directory synchronization jobs/credentials used for identity provisioning. Requires an existing sync topology and additional steps for tenant-wide control.

Can manage PIM eligible/active assignments for privileged access groups.
Broader variant of directory role management read/write across Microsoft 365 services.
Can push apps/scripts and issue remote actions to all Intune-managed devices — fleet-wide code execution, but not a direct tenant takeover path.
Can manage Intune role-based access control assignments.

Full control over all SharePoint site collections. Data-plane access; not a direct tenant takeover path.
Read/write access to all SharePoint site collections.
Can read and write all Teams chat messages across the organization.
